# Inside the Xiān restoration: what the marks recover
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Xiān** is what the evidence put back.

Xiān mythology is a vast gallery of individual adepts, each with a distinctive method of transcendence. They are less a pantheon than a community of perfected beings. The most famous xiān are the Eight Immortals, each representing a different social type and a different path to transcendence.  Zhōnglí Quán was a general; Lǚ Dòngbīn a scholar; Hé Xiāngū a woman who nourished her spirit; Lán Cǎihé a gender-ambiguous beggar; and so on.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Xiān
- **ASCII form:** xian
- **Meaning:** "Immortal"
- **Domain of influence:** Immortal, Transcendent
- **Pantheon:** Chinese
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 仙
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 264 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **仙**. On the evidence, it means "Immortal".

Strip **Xiān** to *xian* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **a → ā** — Long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

None of these marks is decoration. Each one is a fact about how the name was spoken, and each one is checkable against the scholarly record the temple cites.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Xiān** lives at [/sites/xian/](/sites/xian/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/xian/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/xian/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/xian/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Xiān** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Biotech, Longevity & Life Sciences** — The immortals; longevity research’s Taoist proof of concept.
- **Faith & Spiritual Organizations** — Immortality cultivation as a living Taoist path.
- **Yoga, Meditation & Holistic Wellness** — The immortals who perfected breath, diet, and cultivation.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Chinese tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Tao Te Ching](/texts/tao-te-ching/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/xian/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
